---
title: "4 · Quantum Dynamics & Chaos"
---

Random matrices describe a chaotic spectrum at rest. This part puts the system
**in motion** and asks how an initially local piece of information spreads — the
process called **scrambling**.

Two complementary diagnostics appear again and again:

- **Out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs).** The squared commutator
  $C(t) = \langle |[W(t), V]|^2\rangle$ measures how a once-distant operator
  $W(t)$ grows to overlap $V$. Its early-time growth defines a quantum Lyapunov
  exponent, capped by the Maldacena–Shenker–Stanford bound $\lambda \le 2\pi k_B T/\hbar$.
- **The spectral form factor (SFF).** A Fourier transform of the spectrum whose
  *dip–ramp–plateau* shape is the time-domain signature of level repulsion, with a
  plateau pinned at the Hilbert-space dimension.

A third, basis-independent view — **Krylov complexity** — recasts operator growth
as a particle hopping along a semi-infinite chain built by the Lanczos algorithm,
turning "how chaotic" into "how fast does the wavepacket spread."

## Notebooks in this part

- [The $C$–$F$ identity](../notebooks/ch4/solution_ch4_commutator_fidelity_identity.ipynb) — linking the squared commutator to an OTOC fidelity.
- [The spectral form factor](../notebooks/ch4/solution_ch4_spectral_form_factor_plateau.ipynb) — dip, ramp, and the plateau at $K = D$.
- [Krylov complexity](../notebooks/ch4/solution_ch4_krylov_complexity.ipynb) — operator growth as a tight-binding chain, with $\mathcal{C}_K(t) = \sinh^2(\alpha t)$.
